records.reason: Fused carbonyl graph at 2/1 with high sample volume and a broad supplied prediction width. It anchors topology, loading, and carbonyl retention in a sparse region.
Acetophenone-type graph at 5/1 and low volume. It provides a moderate-strength carbonyl reference for condition interpolation among common aromatic ketones.
Fused ester at 20/1 with broad supplied V1/V2 widths. It samples a weak-eluent endpoint where condition response and V2 tail behavior are uncertain.
Oxygen-rich aldehyde graph at 2/1, high loading, and broad predicted endpoints. It targets the recurrent oxygenated V2-tail region and loading interaction.
Small oxygenated ester at 5/1 with a broad prediction and PE loading solvent. It tests whether multi-acceptor structures show endpoint broadening distinct from a simple retention shift.
Halogenated acetophenone at 10/1. It is a compact carbonyl/halogen anchor for interpolating condition response across common aromatic ketones.
Secondary alcohol graph at 5/1 with high predicted onset and broad endpoint range. It probes donor accessibility and V2 broadening in an alcohol family.
The acetophenone-type graph at 1/1 and high loading supplies a controlled condition/loading reference for comparison with the 5/1 point.
Heavy halogenated donor-free graph at 20/1. It supplies a sparse hydrophobic/heavy-atom anchor for testing topology and mass transfer beyond LogP.
Compact bromoanisole-type graph at 2/1 with narrow predicted onset. It calibrates ordinary donor-free ether behavior against more extreme oxygenated rows.
Fused diketone-like graph at 20/1 with substantial supplied V1/V2 widths. It probes fused carbonyl transfer at a weak eluent and moderate loading.
Diaryl ketone at 50/1 has one of the broadest supplied prediction ranges. Its label can repair late-retention and endpoint calibration for aromatic carbonyls.
Highly oxygenated brominated ester at 0/1. It supplies a strong-eluent boundary condition for multi-acceptor structures and tests whether the model exaggerates early retention.
Fused ether at 1/1 provides a compact fused heteroatom anchor with low predicted width. It helps distinguish fused topology from broader carbonyl families.
Fluorinated diketone-like graph at 2/1 and high loading. It samples a carbonyl-rich region where V1 and V2 may respond differently to loading.
Simple aromatic aldehyde at 2/1. It provides a lower-complexity carbonyl anchor for separating aldehyde topology from extreme multi-acceptor V2 tails.
Amino ester at 2/1 with a broad predicted V2 range. It probes whether accessible nitrogen changes carbonyl transfer and endpoint width relative to neutral esters.
Hydroxy-methoxy aromatic aldehyde at 2/1 with high loading. It tests donor accessibility and carbonyl topology in an oxygenated graph with broad predicted endpoints.
Dihalogenated donor-free aromatic graph at 20/1. It expands heavy-atom and hydrophobic coverage at a weak eluent without relying on a universal polarity correction.
Oxygenated aldehyde side-chain graph at 20/1 with very broad supplied predictions. It is a high-value V2-tail and condition-response anchor.
Nitrile-containing aromatic graph at 0/1. It supplies a strong-eluent nitrogen anchor that helps separate nitrile behavior from other nitrogen environments.
Halogenated aromatic ester at 10/1 and low volume. It supplies a nitrogen-free comparison point for distinguishing ester and halogen effects from amino-esters.
Simple donor-free diaryl graph at 0/1. It calibrates strong-eluent behavior for nonpolar aromatic systems and supports transfer to substituted analogues.
Fused ester graph at 5/1 and high loading complements its 20/1 point. The pair tests condition slope and V2 broadening.
Amino ester graph at 20/1 and low volume complements the 10/1 amino-ester point. This contrast can distinguish nitrogen-specific retention from loading effects.
Multi-acceptor aliphatic ester at 2/1 and PE loading solvent. It supplies a lower-complexity endpoint anchor for oxygenated response and loading transfer.
Difluoro aromatic aldehyde at 2/1. It adds a compact halogen/carbonyl anchor to improve interpolation across aldehyde and halogenated carbonyl graphs.
Dibrominated aromatic aldehyde at 1/1. It provides a strong-eluent heavy-atom carbonyl reference for separating halogen and aldehyde effects.
Flexible-chain aldehyde at 10/1 and high loading with broad predicted endpoints. It tests chain size, loading, and carbonyl V2 tails together.
Long-chain acrylate-type ester at 1/1. It adds a hydrophobic chain-size reference to distinguish ester topology and chain effects from highly oxygenated carbonyl tails.
Perfluoroaryl graph at 5/1. It supplies a donor-free fluorinated anchor for testing whether unusual hydrophobicity and halogenation transfer separately from ordinary aromatic rows.
Methoxy aromatic ketone at 2/1 and PE loading solvent. It provides a moderate-condition ether/carbonyl anchor for separating simple ether effects from aldehyde and ester tails.

hypotheses.content: Donor-free aromatic and hydrophobic graphs have condition responses that depend on packing and graph topology beyond LogP and molecular size.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Topology and heavy-atom anchors can reduce transfer errors among common donor-free aromatic rows where descriptor-only corrections are insufficient.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After controlling PE/EA and loading, do fused topology and heavy-atom substitution explain residual retention differences better than size and LogP?

hypotheses.content: Oxygenated and carbonyl-rich structures often have endpoint-specific V2 tails that are underfit even when V1 is closer.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched carbonyl, ester, aldehyde, and multi-acceptor points can teach endpoint-specific broadening rather than a uniform retention offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which combinations of carbonyl topology, donor accessibility, fused structure, and loading produce broad V2 independently of V1?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing rows require graph-conditioned transfer; nitriles, anilines, pyridines, and fused aromatic bases do not share one correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The candidate pool contains chemically distinct nitrogen environments with different predicted condition responses. Graph-specific anchors can prevent a blanket nitrogen correction from degrading generalization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can the retrained graph model separate nitrogen accessibility and basicity from formal acceptor count and aromaticity?

hypotheses.content: High-CW-distance and sparse heteroatom or fused graphs are transfer-failure regions where local anchors improve generalization more than generic novelty alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Rare graph environments can have large residuals despite moderate descriptor similarity, so local structural anchors should repair extrapolation into uncovered regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are high-CW residuals shared across rare heteroatom classes, or does each graph environment need a separate correction?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount changes V1 and V2 differently and the interaction is family-specific.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Loading contrasts let the retrained model learn onset shifts and V2 broadening as separate, family-dependent effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Within each chemical family, does loading primarily shift onset, broaden completion, or change both effects with PE/EA?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback reinforced that a universal late-retention correction is unsafe. Donor-free anchors can be close, while basic aromatic nitrogen, amino-nitrile, and several oxygenated carbonyl graphs remain severe failure regions. Carbonyl and ester outcomes continue to show asymmetric V2 errors, and loading changes the two endpoints differently. The corrected batch therefore emphasizes legal condition contrasts for fused esters and common aromatic ketones, broad carbonyl and oxygenated candidates, nitrogen and heteroatom anchors, and donor-free topology references.
batch_rationale: The batch combines controlled response-curve experiments with broader coverage. Same-graph contrasts at different PE/EA ratios and loadings can identify condition slopes and endpoint-specific loading effects. Broad predicted regions receive oxygenated, carbonyl, ester, and fused anchors, while donor-free and halogenated rows improve transfer among common aromatic structures. The resulting labels should repair failure regions and improve interpolation across the Row-distribution after retraining.
